_note: Tape playback strip, stacked below the footer. Frame 2560x360; the deck offsets these by 1440+420=1860 into the combined 2560x2220 frame. Cut with: punch.py --frame 2560x360 --detect --generic --min-area 900 --max-aspect 9 --threshold 10. Threshold 10 is load bearing -- the wound tape reads at luma 12-21 and the apertures are true #000000, so a looser cutoff punches holes in the tape itself.
_rotary: rotary and rotaryInner are NOT punched holes -- the artwork is opaque there. They are the two concentric hit zones of the painted ROTARY knob, listed here so they inherit apRect() and the +1860 strip offset like everything else. The knob's measured geometry, in this frame's coordinates: centre 2441.5,197.5; inner face out to r=25; body out to r=40. Both boxes are deliberately larger than the paint -- at the size this strip renders the outer ring is about six screen pixels wide, which is not a click target, so the zones extend onto bare panel around it. Their painted index marks were erased by unmark_knob.py and are redrawn live by the deck.
_transport: tRew/tStop/tPlay/tFf are the four TRANSPORT keys, also painted rather than punched. The slots tile the key bank with no dead zone between them -- boundaries sit on the measured dark gaps at x=2170, 2234, 2295 -- and run y=124-242, the key caps. Functions follow the printed legend row above the keys (rewind, stop, play, fast-forward), not the key caps themselves, which the art got wrong: two of them show a rewind arrow and one an eject arrow.
